preamble: The open-mid front vowel [ɛ] lowers to the near-open [æ]. In North American English it is part of the low-back-merger (California) shift, where the retraction of TRAP lets DRESS fall toward [æ], so that bet and wreck approach bat and rack, and in the Inland North DRESS backs and lowers toward [ɐ] or almost [æ]. In Swedish, /ɛ/ and /ɛː/ are lowered to [æ, æː] before /r/ (ära [ˈæ̂ːra] 'honour'), and younger Stockholm speakers extend the lowering to other contexts. In everyday Lithuanian, long [ɛː] shifts to [æː] before a non-palatalized consonant (retas [ˈrʲæːtɐs] 'rare').

examples.note: California Vowel Shift: /ɛ/ is pulled toward [æ] as /æ/ moves toward [ä].
Stressed /ɛ, ɛː/ are lowered to [æ, æː] before /r/ (synchronic allophony).
Speakers born from about 1980 lower /ɛː/ outside the pre-rhotic context too.
In everyday speech long [ɛː] shifts to [æː] before a non-palatalized consonant; short vowels are not affected.
